inputs.goal: Renting a flat in Berlin, viewing with the agent, I have a small dog

findings.detail: scene 1: must_say 8 «ask by when a decision is expected» — slot «the time point» is what the answer names (time)

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: You are meeting a letting agent in Berlin to view a flat you might rent. This is the first in-person contact at the property, and you need to understand the practical basics before deciding whether to apply.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Agent.
Not in this scene: asking whether a dog is allowed, discussing documents in detail, arranging what happens after approval.
must_say: say you are here for the viewing — slot: the flat
give your name — slot: the name
ask whether you may look around first — slot: none
ask about the rent and extra costs — slot: the cost item
ask what is included in the flat — slot: the item
ask how the application process works — slot: none
confirm your interest in the flat — slot: the flat
ask by when a decision is expected — slot: the time point
must_understand: asks for your name and which viewing you are here for
says you can look around and asks if you have questions
says the rent, extra costs and deposit
explains what is included and how the application process works
tells you when the landlord or agent expects to decide

scenes.teaches_native: ask if a dog is allowed
scenes.topic_description:
Situation: During the viewing, the decision may depend on whether the landlord accepts pets. You have a small dog, so this is the key moment to raise it clearly, understand the rules, and learn what information the agent needs.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Agent.
Not in this scene: basic viewing logistics, general rent details, submitting the full application or arranging contract signing.
must_say: ask whether something is allowed — slot: the thing (a dog, a cat)
explain who will live in the flat — slot: the person or pet
ask whether there are rules about something — slot: the thing (pets, noise)
ask whether there is an extra cost for something — slot: the thing (a dog, pet permission)
ask whether the landlord needs more information about something — slot: the thing (the dog, pet references)
answer whether something is calm or trained — slot: the quality
explain how often something would be there alone — slot: the length of time
confirm you understand the condition — slot: the condition
must_understand: asks what kind of pet you have and how big it is
asks whether the pet is quiet, trained or left alone often
says whether pets are allowed and under what conditions
explains whether the landlord needs extra information or approval
tells you about any extra rules or costs related to pets

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: After the viewing, you decide to apply for the flat. The agent explains the application stage, and you need to understand the required documents, how to send them, and what timeline to expect after the viewing.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Agent.
Not in this scene: first impressions of the flat, pet permission itself, negotiating rent or discussing the final contract.
must_say: say you want to apply for the flat — slot: the flat
ask which documents are required — slot: none
ask how you should send the documents — slot: the method
ask by when the documents are needed — slot: the deadline
explain what document you already have — slot: the document
ask whether a document from another country is accepted — slot: the document
ask whom to contact about an update — slot: the contact person
confirm when you will send everything — slot: the time point
must_understand: says which documents are required for the application
explains how and when to send the documents
asks whether you already have the standard documents
says whether documents from another country are accepted
tells you who will contact you and when
